rows.text: The prepared native reasoner currently has to be consumed to obtain its proof checking context. A caller retaining one prepared source for repeated decisions cannot borrow that same immutable context for checking; it must give up the reasoner or prepare another one. This obstructs the shared native store boundary required by downstream logic execution.

Prepared verification must reuse the immutable consumer context identity instead of immediately canonicalizing the whole source a second time. Retain the explicit supplied-source verification boundary, with both forms sharing source/question/trust-base binding and the same replay implementation. The actual validation caller must use prepared verification. Tests must compare complete replay reports across both storage and input choices and reject a different prepared source, wrong question, unprepared query context and stopped caller.

Source inspection after the first runtime checks found that validation canonicalizes the complete source in Reasoner::with_proofs and then immediately repeats it in ServiceProof::verify. Add verify_prepared against the sealed immutable consumer context. Factor source/question/trust-base binding into one helper and retain the existing supplied-source check as an explicit validation boundary using the same replay implementation. The production validation caller will use the prepared path. Owning/borrowed and source/prepared paths must return identical reports, with wrong source context, wrong question, tampered proof and stopping receipt still rejected. This eliminates one duplicate complete-source identity computation per actual validation check; no elapsed-time speedup is claimed without measurement. This strengthens the same prepared-store scope and leaves the larger ownership plan open.
